claim: Raw combined-corpus (TRAIN+VALIDATION+HOLDOUT_FROZEN together) joint mutual information is a valid within-split leakage test.
result: false; a real ~0.276-bit combined-corpus signal in the B1 blueprint v2 leakage audit was entirely explained by the intended HOLDOUT_FROZEN disjoint-symbol-pool design, not a nuisance leak -- caught by chatgpt-secondary, independently reproduced before accepting.

claim: Keying the B1 balanced-TRAIN-tier order-pair selection by (template, triplet) avoids reintroducing a target leak.
result: false; every symbol is triplet-unique so target reveals triplet, which then predicted the surviving order-pair (0.079-0.276 bit leaks measured); a second attempt keying by (class, polarity, layout) also failed (0.585-bit leak, order became a proxy for class); only keying by template alone (provably target-independent) passed.

claim: B6's three cosmetic-filler hash() call sites (Python built-in hash on string tuples) produce reproducible output across process restarts.
result: false; str/tuple hash() is PYTHONHASHSEED-salted per process since Python 3.3 -- verified non-reproducible, then fixed with a hashlib-based stable hash; targets themselves were never affected (cosmetic filler only).

claim: A round-2 scoring rule of the form round1_winner_score + fixed_per_role_offset causally depends on which round-1 candidate won.
result: false; all three offsets share the same base value, so the largest offset always wins regardless of the base -- silently made 0 of 864 GWT_CAUSAL_REENTRY rows test anything about re-entry; fixed with a genuinely conditional per-winner rule, 576/864 rows now distinguishing.

claim: Assigning course-A's cosmetic node_identity field via a hash of (combo, redundancy_requested, hint, split) is nuisance-safe.
result: false; shares ancestry with the target's own determinants, measured 0.0032-bit leak; fixed by making node_identity a strict 1:1 alias of split instead.
